facts.text: The Okanagan tech sector contributes $4.98 billion a year to the local economy and consists of 787 companies supporting 32,645 jobs, nearly $3 billion more than in the 2017 study.
In 2025, Kelowna issued 12,390 business licences, down slightly from a high of 12,515 in 2024, while licensed businesses across the Central Okanagan rose to 17,299 from 16,802.
Kelowna International Airport handled 636,815 passengers in the first quarter of 2026, up about 7.6% from 592,085 in the first quarter of 2025.
Total employment in the Central Okanagan from January to June 2026 was 122,767, up 9.8% from 111,767 over the same period a year earlier.
Kelowna's tourism industry recorded positive results through the second quarter of 2026, with growth in hotel revenue, short-term rental demand and airport passenger volumes.

overview: Kelowna grew 13.5 percent between 2016 and 2021, from 127,390 to 144,576 residents, one of the fastest rates of any Canadian city its size. Its 62,209 occupied dwellings spread over 211.85 square kilometres along Okanagan Lake, the median age is 42.4, and the median household income was $82,000 in 2020.

Technology, tourism, construction and health care drive the economy, and the airport and business licence counts keep rising. For a local business, Kelowna offers a stream of new arrivals who have not yet chosen their providers, a wealthy retiree segment and a seasonal visitor surge that rewards firms ready to capture summer demand.

byService.lead-generation: Because Kelowna grew 13.5 percent between 2016 and 2021, lead generation should prioritize newcomer channels such as movers and real estate partners, plus neighbourhood campaigns in Glenmore, Rutland and the Mission.
byService.seo: Kelowna SEO must beat aggressive competition from tourism and real estate sites, so a business needs Okanagan-specific keywords, seasonal content and location pages for a 211.85 square kilometre city.
byService.website-development: A Kelowna website should load quickly on mobile for visitors and new residents, present pricing plainly for households earning a median of $82,000, and make seasonal booking simple.
byService.branding: With a median age of 42.4 and a lifestyle-driven population, Kelowna branding works when it pairs Okanagan imagery with a credible, modern tone that appeals to both retirees and tech workers.
